approachQuestion.prompt: A warehouse records nonnegative integer quantities, each at most 1,000,000. For each nonempty contiguous interval, its value is the interval sum multiplied by its smallest quantity. Return the largest such value. Example: [2, 3, 2] returns 14 from the full interval; [0, 4, 0] returns 16. All sums and products fit in signed 64-bit arithmetic. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Build prefix sums. For every position, use ordered stacks to find the nearest strictly smaller quantity on each side, popping greater-or-equal values in each directional pass. Evaluate its quantity times the prefix-sum total of the entire span between those boundaries.
options.feedback: All quantities are nonnegative, so extending a span without lowering its minimum cannot decrease its sum or product. Every interval has a minimum position whose widest eligible span is at least as valuable.

options.text: Find each position’s widest minimum-valid span and multiply its quantity by the span length.
options.feedback: Length is not sum. For [2, 3, 2], this gives at most 6, whereas the required product is 2×7=14.

options.text: Multiply the sum of the whole input by its global minimum.
options.feedback: An interval avoiding a zero may be better. For [0, 4, 0], the whole-input product is 0 but [4] gives 16.

options.text: For each left endpoint extend the right endpoint, maintaining sum and minimum and evaluating every interval.
options.feedback: It is correct but evaluates every interval, causing quadratic work. Prefix sums and minimum boundaries avoid that enumeration.

feedback.reason: Combine minimum-valid spans with range sums, using nonnegativity to justify choosing a widest span.
details: Construct prefix sums and strict-smaller boundary arrays with two ordered-stack scans. For each index, subtract prefix sums to obtain the full boundary-delimited span sum, multiply by its quantity, and update the maximum.

With nonnegative quantities, extending within a candidate minimum's strict-smaller boundaries cannot decrease its span sum. Prefix sums obtain that sum directly. Negative quantities would invalidate this maximal-span argument.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For minimum-span-prefix-sum, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the quantity count. Prefix sums, two boundary arrays, and a reused stack are separate working storage. No interval is copied.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build prefixes and boundaries once, then evaluate one full-span contribution per index.
details: All scans and prefix construction take O(n) time; every index is pushed and popped at most once in each stack pass. Prefix sums, boundaries, and the stack occupy O(n) auxiliary space.
